definitions.explanation: Tangible and intangible cultural assets inherited from previous generations, including buildings, art, traditions, and practices. Often used in the context of UNESCO World Heritage.

examples.japanese: ⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧{文化|ぶんか}{遺産|いさん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{登録|とうろく}→登録：05703_touroku⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage site.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{文化|ぶんか}{遺産|いさん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}した→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧。
examples.english: I participated in activities to protect local cultural heritage.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{数多|かずおお}く→数多く：12948_kazuooku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{文化|ぶんか}{遺産|いさん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{観光客|かんこうきゃく}→観光客：03022_kankoukyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れる→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。
examples.english: Japan has numerous cultural heritage sites, and many tourists visit each year.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly used in discussions about preservation, tourism, and UNESCO designations. Japan has many registered World Heritage sites, making this term frequently encountered in travel and culture-related contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧{文化|ぶんか}{遺産|いさん} (World Cultural Heritage)
- {文化|ぶんか}{遺産|いさん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{保護|ほご}→保護：03625_hogo⟧ (protection of cultural heritage)
- {文化|ぶんか}{遺産|いさん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{登録|とうろく}する→登録する：25227_tourokusuru⟧ (to register as cultural heritage)
